blocks.text: מַעֲרִיב לֵיל שֵׁנִי שֶׁל ראשׁ הַשָּׁנָה

עָלֵינוּ לְשַׁבֵּחַ לַאֲדוֹן הַכֹּל לָתֵת גְּדֻלָּה לְיוֹצֵר בְּרֵאשִׁית שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂנוּ כְּגוֹיֵי הָאֲרָצוֹת וְלֹא שָׂמָנוּ כְּמִשְׁפְּחוֹת הָאֲדָמָה שֶׁלֹּא שָׂם חֶלְקֵנוּ כָּהֶם וְגֹרָלֵנוּ כְּכָל־הֲמוֹנָם. וַאֲנַחְנוּ כֹּרְעִים וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוִים וּמוֹדִים לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֶה שָׁמַיִם וְיוֹסֵד אֶרֶץ וּמוֹשַׁב יְקָרוֹ בַּשָּׁמַיִם מִמַּעַל וּשְׁכִינַת עֻזּוֹ בְּגָבְהֵי מְרוֹמִים: הוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֵין עוֹד. אֱמֶת מַלְכֵּנוּ אֶפֶס זוּלָתוֹ. כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתוֹ וְיָדַעְתָּ הַיּוֹם וַהֲשֵׁבֹתָ אֶל־לְבָבֶךָ כִּי יְהוָה הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים בַּשָּׁמַיִם מִמַּעַל וְעַל־הָאָרֶץ מִתָּחַת אֵין עוֹד:

עַל־כֵּן נְקַוֶּה לְּךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לִרְאוֹת מְהֵרָה בְּתִפְאֶרֶת עֻזֶּךָ לְהַעֲבִיר גִּלּוּלִים מִן־הָאָרֶץ וְהָאֱלִילִים כָּרוֹת יִכָּרֵתוּן. לְתַקֵּן עוֹלָם בְּמַלְכוּת שַׁדַּי וְכָל־בְּנֵי בָשָׂר יִקְרְאוּ בִשְׁמֶךָ. לְהַפְנוֹת אֵלֶיךָ כָּל־רִשְׁעֵי אָרֶץ. יַכִּירוּ וְיֵדְעוּ כָּל־יוֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל כִּי לְךָ תִּכְרַע כָּל־בֶּרֶךְ תִּשָּׁבַע כָּל־לָשׁוֹן: לְפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ יִכְרְעוּ וְיִפֹּלוּ. וְלִכְבוֹד שִׁמְךָ יְקָר יִתֵּנוּ. וִיקַבְּלוּ כֻלָּם אֶת־עֹל מַלְכוּתֶךָ. וְתִמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם מְהֵרָה לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. כִּי הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁלְּךָ הִיא וּלְעוֹלְמֵי עַד תִּמְלוֹךְ בְּכָבוֹד. כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ, יְהוָה יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד: וְנֶאֱמַר, וְהָיָה יְיָ לְמֶלֶךְ עַל־כָּל־הָאָרֶץ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיֶה יְיָ אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד:

A short ornamental rule closes the section. There is faint show-through of Latin-script text from the facing or reverse page at the upper right (e.g. "Year") and in the lower margin. It is not part of this page's text.

uncertainties.question: I can't see a holam on the resh, so I transcribed it without one. A small dot over the shin seems to be there. Is a holam present but faint?
Is there a holam over the gimel, or is it a vowel-less ג? The mark is small.
The vowel under the lamed/qof isn't clear (sheva under lamed, tsere under qof?). I followed what I could see.
Is the first vowel a segol or a qamats? There also seems to be an extra mark under/beside the alef that could be a cantillation accent. I couldn't settle it.
There is a small mark before/under the ayin. I read it as a qubbutz. Could it be a stray mark or an accent?
Is there a holam over the vav or he (יְהוָֹה), as is often printed? I can't confirm one, so I left it out.
uncertainties.region: line 10 (Deut. verse) and the כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ line near the bottom

uncertainties.question: There appear to be extra marks under the alef/resh. These could be cantillation accents (the passage is a biblical quotation) or just broken vowel points. I didn't record any accent because I can't identify one with confidence.

uncertainties.question: Is there a dagesh in the lamed, or is it plain לְךָ?
Under several forms of ארץ there are clustered marks that could be an accent (e.g. tipcha/etnachta) or just qamats + segol. I couldn't settle them.
uncertainties.region: paragraph 2, lines 2, 4, and the second-to-last line

uncertainties.question: Is there an extra mark under the resh/alef (sheva vs. a possible accent)?
Is there a dagesh in the kaf (כֻּלָּם)? I couldn't see one.
Is it plene with vav-holam, as transcribed, or defective with holam alone? It looks plene.
Both words look defective (no vav), with a holam dot. I transcribed them that way. Please confirm the dots are holam and not stray marks.

The two Bible quotations (Deut. 4:39, Exod. 15:18, Zech. 14:9) show no clear cantillation at this resolution, apart from the possible marks noted above. Fine meteg strokes may be present but unresolved.

completeness_limitations: I read all four images. The text is fully legible at the consonant level. Vowel points are mostly clear, but some small marks (possible accents, meteg, dagesh, holam in the divine name) can't be settled at this scan resolution, and I listed each one above instead of guessing. I didn't fill in anything from memory of the standard text. There is no German or Rashi-script instruction on this page. The only instruction is the small square-script line 'קַדִּישׁ יָתוֹם, יִגְדַּל.'
